match.reason: No single bank point covers all three kinds of value (environmental, economic, and cultural, spiritual and aesthetic) together; the closest points each cover only one or two of these, so the new point is broader and needs its own card.

draft.title: Ways people use and value water
card: Environmental value
Water keeps ecosystems alive. Rivers, wetlands and lakes give plants and animals a place to live and water to drink.
Economic value
Water helps people make money and goods. Farms use it to grow crops, factories use it to make products, and power stations use it to make electricity.
Cultural, spiritual and aesthetic value
Some water places hold meaning for a community or are loved for their beauty. A lake may be a place of ceremony, or a waterfall may be a place people visit to enjoy the view.
One place can be valued in more than one way. People may value a river for its farms and also for its wildlife and its beauty.
draft.remember: People value water for nature, for money and goods, and for meaning and beauty.

a.q: A town's wetland is home to many birds and frogs. Which value of water does this show?
a.why: The wetland gives birds and frogs a place to live, so it has environmental value for the ecosystem. Aesthetic value is about beauty for people, and the question is about the animals that live there.
a.clue: Think about who or what depends on the water to live.

b.q: Kiran's family grows apples on an orchard in Victoria. They pump water from a river to their trees. They also swim at a nearby river bend each summer because it is so beautiful. Which pair of values does this show?
b.why: Pumping river water to grow apples to sell is an economic value. Swimming at a river bend because it is beautiful is an aesthetic value. The river may also help wildlife, but nothing in the story is about animals or plants living there.
b.clue: Match each action to one value: one is about making goods, the other is about beauty.

problems.detail: The clue says 'one is about making goods, the other is about beauty'. These are the card's own wording for economic and aesthetic value, so the clue all but names the answer pair and a student needs no reasoning about the story.
